title: The Price of the Fifth Page
next_chapter_hook: Chen Ji's finger hovered above the fifth page, cold sweat soaking through his back—he had already used up three chances, and the hourglass of fate was quietly running out where he could not see.

text.content:
The moment the light curtain twisted, Chen Ji felt as if he were being watched by an invisible giant eye. That gaze pierced through his flesh, bloodline, and Mental Sea, reaching the deepest part of his soul—where the Tianji Record Fragment lay hidden, his final trump card.

"Awakened..."

He murmured to himself, his voice dry as withered leaves rubbing together. The burning sensation in his chest reminded him that the presence had already sensed his existence. Mo Xiansheng was right—the Heavenly Eye had never been sleeping; it was merely waiting.

Just as Chen Ji prepared to forcibly extinguish the light curtain, an aged voice rang out from the Void: "Friend, pray wait."

Cang Yutian—that name which should have scattered into the long river of history, manifested before Chen Ji in the form of a remnant soul. His features were blurred like a reflection in water, but those eyes were crystal clear, so deep they seemed to hold the rise and fall of an entire universe.

dialogue.content:
"You've come this far, and some truths must be told."

Cang Yutian's voice carried not a trace of emotional fluctuation. "The fifth page is called 'Fate Writing.' It can rewrite established causality, resurrect dead ends, and turn certain defeat into victory. This is the final forbidden power of the Tianji Record, and also the abyss where generations of inheritors fell."

text.content:
Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. Fate Writing—these four words struck his heart like a heavy hammer. He recalled the three times he had wielded the fifth page's power in desperate moments, each time turning peril into safety, each time believing it was the Tianji Record's grace.

But now he understood: that was not grace, it was a loan.

dialogue.content:
"Each time you write fate, a corner of the timeline collapses."

Cang Yutian waved his hand, and countless interwoven rays of light appeared in the Void, like a shattered spiderweb. "Look—these are the prices you paid for rewriting causality. The originally clear main path has been twisted and forked, and each collapse..."

He paused, his voice carrying a hint of compassion for the first time: "...accelerates the awakening of the Heavenly Eye."

text.content:
Chen Ji felt a bone-deep chill rise from his tailbone straight to his crown. He subconsciously calculated rapidly in his mind—

The first time, the lethal trap formation at Qingyun Peak, he rewrote a certain death.
The second time, the pursuit by Xuanwu Sect genius Han Lie, he reversed the battle situation.
The third time... when was the third time?

His fingers trembled slightly as a terrifying thought surfaced: he could not remember when he had used it the third time. What did this mean? Had the collapse of the timeline already begun to erode his memories?

"When will the Heavenly Eye fully awaken?" Chen Ji's voice was eerily calm—that was his expression only when极度nervous, the more he could suppress all emotions.

Cang Yutian extended a虚幻 finger and gently tapped the light curtain. A crack spread from the curtain's edge, like spiderweb patterns on ice struck by a stone. "When the fifth page is completely filled, your timeline will collapse entirely, and it... will come personally to reap."

choice.prompt: Chen Ji stared intently at the crack, his voice low: "How many chances do I have left?"

choices.description: Without concealing his urgency, facing the harsh truth—even if that number might drive him to despair.
choices.visible_reward: Obtaining complete information to provide a basis for subsequent decisions
choices.risk_hint: The truth may be crueler than anticipated

text.content: Cang Yutian fell silent for a moment, and something like an expression flickered across that blurred face. "Three." His voice was soft. "You have three chances left. After that, the Book of Fate will close automatically, and the Heavenly Eye... will follow your collapsed timeline and come personally."

choices.text: Questioning the authenticity of the information
choices.description: With his usual caution, suspecting this is some kind of test or trap—why would Cang Yutian help him?
choices.visible_reward: Probing the other party's hand, confirming motives

dialogue.content:
"Why tell me this?" Chen Ji's gaze was like a blade. "You and I have never crossed paths. What benefit is the Heavenly Eye's awakening to you?"

Cang Yutian let out a low laugh, a laugh carrying inexplicable bitterness: "Because I don't want to see a second 'me.' Back then, I abused Fate Writing and ended up with my soul scattered to the winds, not even having a chance for revenge."

choices.description: He never puts all his hopes on one path—there must be another way, there must be a possibility he hasn't considered.
choices.visible_cost: Exposing his urgent mindset of seeking an escape route
choices.visible_reward: Might obtain key clues or hidden information
choices.risk_hint: Cang Yutian might use this to probe his cards

text.content:
Chen Ji did not directly respond to that number, but asked: "If I don't use the fifth page, letting fate develop along its original trajectory?"

Cang Yutian's answer came quickly: "Then you will perish in the final showdown. The Tianji Record's mission is to break the cycle, not to witness it repeat." He paused. "Besides... your sister is still in the Holy Sect's hands."

Chen Nian.

That name was like a red-hot iron needle, pierced mercilessly into Chen Ji's heart. His sister, the girl taken by the Holy Sect and made into the "Heavenly Fate Lock Key," was the greatest weakness that drove him onto this road of no return.

If he did not win in the final showdown, Chen Nian would forever become a sacrifice in the Heavenly Chess Game.

But if he exhausted all three chances on the fifth page, the timeline would collapse entirely, and everything he cared about—including Chen Nian—would turn to nothingness along with him.

"The final showdown... when does it come?"

When Chen Ji asked this question, his voice remained calm. Only he knew that beneath that calmness was a raging storm of calculations and weighings. He was rapidly estimating every variable, every possibility.

Cang Yutian raised his illusory palm, and a map appeared in the Void. "The day the Ancient Forbidden Land opens, that is when the showdown comes. And the entrance to the Forbidden Land..." His voice became meaningful. "Only appears when Heavenly Fate drops below the critical threshold."

Chen Ji's heart sank heavily.

Heavenly Fate Value—that was what he consumed each time he used the Tianji Record's foresight ability. 5 points for one glimpse, the next three hours. His current Heavenly Fate Value...

He quickly flipped through his memory. Initial: one hundred points. Used once at Qingyun Peak, minus five. Used twice during the Xuanwu Sect pursuit, minus ten. Used three times in the conflicts with Su Qingyao...

Remaining: seventy-two points.

And the critical threshold for the Forbidden Land's opening—fifty points.

dialogue.content:
"You're calculating." Cang Yutian seemed to see through his thoughts. "That's right—the Forbidden Land's entrance only opens to the 'near-dead.' When you drop below fifty points, the Forbidden Land will respond to your call and open. And by then..."

He extended three fingers: "You must have all three chances planned out before then. Where to use them, when to use them—any misstep means utter destruction."

text.content:
Twenty-two points of leeway.

Chen Ji carved this number into the deepest part of his mind. At his current rate of consumption, every glimpse of the future would bring him one step closer to the Forbidden Land. In other words, he had to meticulously calculate the use of every single one of his remaining four foresight opportunities.

One to find clues about Chen Nian.
One to scout intelligence about the final showdown.
The remaining two... as survival backup.

But was this truly the optimal solution?

choice.prompt: "Senior Cang Yutian," Chen Ji lifted his eyes to直视 that illusory figure, "how did you plan it back then? Is there a path to success?"

choices.description: The path Cang Yutian walked might have something worthwhile—even in failure, lessons can be drawn.
choices.visible_cost: Consumes time, Cang Yutian might not reveal everything
choices.risk_hint: Predecessor's experience may not apply to the present

dialogue.content:
Cang Yutian fell silent for a long while, and something like a flicker of light passed through those deep eyes. "I was... too arrogant back then." His voice was low. "I used my first chance to save an inconsequential person, my second to pursue and kill an enemy, and my third..."

He didn't finish, but that silence was answer enough.

choices.description: His chess game has never faltered—he doesn't need advice from a failure, even if that person once wielded the same power.
choices.risk_hint: Blind confidence may lead to repeating past mistakes

text.content:
Chen Ji slightly shook his head, a hint of cold indifference curving his lips. "I've noted your lessons, Senior. But my chess game is different from yours."

Cang Yutian did not rebut, only letting out a meaningful sigh: "May it be so. But remember—between chess player and chess piece, there is often only a thin line."

Chen Ji carved these words into his heart. Chess player and chess piece, a thin line.

He suddenly recalled what Mo Xiansheng had said: "Every master of the Tianji Record believed themselves the one holding the pieces. But in the end, they discovered they were merely the brightest piece on the board."

Back then he dismissed it as an old man's fearmongering; now he saw every word cut to the bone.

"One more thing." Cang Yutian's form began to grow increasingly illusory, as if about to dissipate into the Void at any moment. "The consequences of hastily using the fifth page are more severe than you imagine."

His voice became ethereal: "By 'haste,' I mean wielding Fate Writing while emotionally agitated or mentally confused. At such times, your will cannot control that power, and what you rewrite will be completely out of control—mild deviation from the target, or worse..."

He didn't finish, but Chen Ji already understood.

Worse—the timeline would collapse in ways he could not foresee, and even the Heavenly Eye would not need to act personally.

choice.prompt: The light curtain began to dissipate, Cang Yutian's form growing ever more illusory. Before vanishing completely, he cast one final glance at Chen Ji—that gaze held an indescribable meaning.

choices.description: The more critical the moment, the more he must suppress his emotions. Every move he makes is the result of careful consideration—he will never lose the entire game due to a momentary impulse.

text.content:
Chen Ji took a deep breath, pressing all emotions into the deepest recesses of his heart. He closed his eyes, rapidly constructing a massive chessboard in his mind.

Chen Nian, Han Lie, Su Qingyao, Ye Qing, Ling Yuan... every person was a piece, every step must be precisely calculated.

Three chances. Twenty-two points of leeway. The time window for the Forbidden Land's opening.

He slowly opened his eyes, his pupils reflecting the dissipating light curtain, a cold and ruthless arc curving his lips: "Interesting."

choices.description: Chen Nian's figure surfaced in his mind. That sister, whom he had sent into danger with his own hands after years of separation, was now waiting in some dark corner for rescue.
choices.visible_reward: Reinforcing sense of purpose, clarifying core motivation
choices.risk_hint: Emotional fluctuations may be exploited by those with ulterior motives

text.content:
The instant the light curtain completely vanished, Chen Ji's shoulders sagged slightly.

Just a moment.

He remembered many years ago, Chen Nian tugging at his robe, saying in her childish voice, "Brother will protect me, right?" He had nodded without hesitation, believing that as long as he was strong enough, he could keep her safe for a lifetime.

But everything that happened afterward taught him that fate never shows mercy simply because of your promises.

"I'll get you out." He silently vowed in his heart. "Even if it means opposing all of heaven."

The light curtain fully dissipated, and the room sank back into darkness. Chen Ji sat alone on the简陋 bed, moonlight streaming through the broken window lattice, casting mottled shadows across his face.

Three chances.

He silently calculated the remaining opportunities in his heart. Every use had to be precise to the millimeter. Any deviation, and the timeline would collapse in ways he could not anticipate.

What troubled him even more was that from now on, every glimpse of the future would consume his remaining Heavenly Fate Value, pushing him step by step toward the critical threshold for the Forbidden Land's opening.

His time was shorter than he imagined.

Just then, soft knocking came from the door.

"Brother Chen?"

It was Su Qingyao's voice. Chen Ji's eyes slightly narrowed, swiftly concealing all emotional fluctuations, donning once more the mask of cowardice and mediocrity.

"Come in." His voice returned to its usual weakness and dullness, as if that person who had just borne a shocking secret alone in the darkness had never existed.

The door creaked open, and Su Qingyao's cold visage appeared in the moonlight. Her gaze lingered on Chen Ji for a moment, sensing something unusual but unable to pinpoint it.

"It's so late—something wrong?" Chen Ji kept his head lowered, his tone carrying just the right amount of fear.

dialogue.content:
"The Sect Master summons." Su Qingyao's tone was as cold as ever, but those eyes carried a hint of scrutiny. "Regarding the Sect Competition three days from now."

Chen Ji's heart tightened. Sect Competition—that was the trap Ling Yuan had specially set for him. On the surface a competition, in reality a hunt targeting this "waste."

He lifted his head, revealing a timid smile: "I... I will be there on time."

Su Qingyao did not leave immediately. She quietly gazed at Chen Ji, a complex light flickering in her eyes. After a long while, she turned to leave, leaving behind a meaningful remark: "Some things cannot be hidden merely by pretending."

text.content:
Footsteps faded into the distance, and the timid smile on Chen Ji's face slowly faded away, replaced by an abyssal chill.

Su Qingyao... that woman was too sharp. From the day she entered the Sect, she never truly believed he was a waste. Three times approaching the truth, three times deflected by him, yet she still hadn't given up.

This was both a threat and an opportunity.

Chen Ji rose, walking to the window, gazing in the direction Su Qingyao had departed. At the Sect Competition three days later, Ling Yuan would undoubtedly stir things up behind the scenes. And he... needed that very competition to verify certain of his own arrangements.

But now, everything had to be recalculated.

He reached out, gently pressing on the burning spot over his heart. There, the fifth page of the Tianji Record was faintly warm, as if reminding him: time is passing, fate is counting down.

Three chances.

He must complete all his arrangements within these three opportunities. Find Chen Nian, defeat Ling Yuan, oppose the Heavenly Eye...

Every step is a game of life and death, every step permits not the slightest miscalculation.

Under the moonlight, Chen Ji slowly closed his eyes. When he opened them again, his pupils held only ice-cold calculation.

"Come then." He murmured, his voice betraying no emotion whatsoever. "Let me see—where, in the end, does this game conclude..."

And in the depths of the Void unseen by Chen Ji, a pair of enormous eyes slowly opened.

Those eyes had no pupils, only endless chaos and darkness. They did not look at Chen Ji, but at the timeline slowly collapsing beneath his feet.

"Interesting..."

A low murmur echoed through the Void, carrying an indescribable meaning.

"It's been a long time since this game has been so interesting."

Those eyes closed again, as if they had never opened. But if one could see the changes in the timeline, they would discover—

The line where Chen Ji stood had become thinner still.
